name: Three-Line Strike Traded Against Its Name
note: Three same-coloured bars making monotonic progress -- rising closes AND rising lows, each with a body at least bmin of its own range, in the direction the EMA(10) already says -- then one bar of at least rmin x ATR(14) that closes back through `erase` of everything the run achieved, measured from close(C) to open(A). Bulkowski's 4.7-million-line census says this resolves AGAINST its textbook label in both directions (the bullish strike is a bearish reversal 65% of the time, the bearish strike a bullish one 84%), so the trade is taken opposite the pattern's name. Two knobs exist because the pattern is defined on daily bars and this study runs intraday. `erase` = 1.0 is the textbook full erasure and is in the sweep, but on 5-minute bars one bar undoing three strong ones is close to nonexistent, so the default asks for most of the run rather than all of it. `gap` switches the open(D)-beyond-close(C) condition on: intraday, consecutive opens sit on the prior close, so that clause stops meaning 'opened against the run and reversed' and becomes a coin-flip on one tick -- it is off by default and swept, not silently dropped. Optional 3-bar entry delay, no target, a 10-bar time stop: the claimed edge is in the tail, not the median.
source: Bulkowski, Encyclopedia of Candlestick Charts; https://thepatternsite.com/ThreeLineStrikeBull.html (rank 2/103, frequency rank 95, bearish reversal 65%, n=69, 'wait 3 days before selling after downward breakouts in uptrends') and https://thepatternsite.com/ThreeLineStrikeBear.html (overall rank 1/103, bullish reversal 84%, n=85).
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    ctx.a = ctx.indicator("atr", period=int(ctx.p.atr_n))
    ctx.e = ctx.indicator("ema", period=int(ctx.p.ema_n))


def _body_ok(o, h, l, c, bmin):
    r = h - l
    if r <= 0:
        return False
    return abs(c - o) >= bmin * r


def signal(ctx, i):
    j = i - int(ctx.p.delay)
    if j < 3:
        return 0
    a = ctx.a[j]
    e = ctx.e[j]
    if a is None or e is None or a <= 0:
        return 0
    bmin = float(ctx.p.bmin)
    rmin = float(ctx.p.rmin)
    er = float(ctx.p.erase)
    gap = int(ctx.p.gap)
    A, B, C, D = j - 3, j - 2, j - 1, j

    oA, hA, lA, cA = ctx.o[A], ctx.h[A], ctx.l[A], ctx.c[A]
    oB, hB, lB, cB = ctx.o[B], ctx.h[B], ctx.l[B], ctx.c[B]
    oC, hC, lC, cC = ctx.o[C], ctx.h[C], ctx.l[C], ctx.c[C]
    oD, hD, lD, cD = ctx.o[D], ctx.h[D], ctx.l[D], ctx.c[D]

    if (hD - lD) < rmin * a:
        return 0
    if not (_body_ok(oA, hA, lA, cA, bmin) and _body_ok(oB, hB, lB, cB, bmin)
            and _body_ok(oC, hC, lC, cC, bmin)):
        return 0

    # ---- the BULLISH three-line strike. Bulkowski's census says it resolves
    # DOWN 65% of the time, so it is sold, not bought.
    if cA > oA and cB > oB and cC > oC \
            and cA < cB < cC and lA < lB < lC and cC > e \
            and cD < oD and (not gap or oD > cC) \
            and cD <= cC - er * (cC - oA):
        return -1

    # ---- the BEARISH three-line strike: up 84% of the time. Bought.
    if cA < oA and cB < oB and cC < oC \
            and cA > cB > cC and hA > hB > hC and cC < e \
            and cD > oD and (not gap or oD < cC) \
            and cD >= cC + er * (oA - cC):
        return 1
    return 0
